text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is diagnosed when your blood pressure readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.

Blood pressure is measured with two numbers: systolic (the top number, which measures pressure when your heart beats) and diastolic (the bottom number, which measures pressure when your heart rests between beats).
According to the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, blood pressure is categorized as follows: www.heart.org +1

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic

Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180/120 mm Hg (Seek immediate medical attention if accompanied by symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, or vision changes).
The "Silent Killer": Most people with high blood pressure have no noticeable symptoms or warning signs. Regular checks are the only way to know your numbers.

Lifestyle and Treatment: Stage 1 hypertension is often managed first with heart-healthy lifestyle changes (such as reducing sodium, exercising, and weight management), though medication may be added based on your overall cardiovascular risk. Stage 2 hypertension typically requires both lifestyle changes and medication.
